html:
A Hindu power of western India, founded by Shivaji in 1674, that became the leading Indian power of the 1700s before falling to the British in 1818.

The Marathas were Marathi-speaking warriors and farmers of the western Deccan. Shivaji rebelled against the sultanate of Bijapur and the Mughal Empire, seized hill forts, fought with fast light cavalry, and in 1674 was crowned king at Raigad. After his death the emperor Aurangzeb spent his last twenty-five years trying to crush the Marathas and failed.

After 1707 power passed from Shivaji's heirs to their chief ministers, the Peshwas, who ruled from Pune. Under Baji Rao I in the 1720s and 1730s Maratha armies swept north into central India and to the gates of Delhi. They collected a quarter of the revenue, the chauth, from regions they did not rule directly.

The state became a confederacy. Under the Peshwa, great families ran their own realms:

  • the Scindias of Gwalior,
  • the Holkars of Indore,
  • the Gaekwads of Baroda,
  • the Bhonsles of Nagpur.

In 1761 the Afghan ruler Ahmad Shah Durrani crushed a Maratha army at the Third Battle of Panipat, one of the bloodiest battles of the century. The Marathas recovered, and Mahadji Scindia controlled the Mughal emperor in Delhi in the 1780s. But the chiefs quarrelled, and in three Anglo-Maratha Wars the East India Company defeated them one by one. In 1818 the last Peshwa surrendered, and the Company became the paramount power in India.
sum: A Hindu power of western India, founded by Shivaji in 1674, that became the leading Indian power of the 1700s before falling to the British in 1818.
